title: Definition document
description: The body of a workflow definition: section 3 of the run contract. The daemon validates a posted body against this schema and against the Rust validator in crates/mcpd-runs, and refuses one the walker could not run with a 400 that names the field. Unknown fields are refused everywhere, so a guard that is spelled wrong is an error and not a run that skips its guard. The rules this schema cannot express are the validator's: ids unique within the document, which roots a path may read at its position, a `matches` pattern that compiles.

input_schema.description: An optional JSON Schema for the run's input. A run started with an input that fails it is a 400. Absent means any input.

limits.description: The ceilings on the run. Every one is optional.

steps.description: The nodes, walked in array order. That order is the whole of the ordering rule: there are no edges and no `after` in version 1, and a guard that needs an earlier result reads `steps.<id>`.

output.description: An optional template rendered when the run reaches the end of the graph and stored on the run.

Id.description: A step id: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and underscores, so every generator can turn it into an identifier.

Path.description: A path into the context a node sees: dot-separated names with `[n]` for array positions, such as `input.order.lines[0].sku`. The roots are `input`, `steps.<id>`, `run`, and inside a `foreach` body `item` and `index`, inside a `loop` body `iter.index`. A path that names nothing reads as null.

TemplateString.description: A string in which every `${path}` is replaced by the value the path names: a string verbatim, a number or bool as JSON, an object or array as compact JSON, null as an empty string. A string that is exactly one `${path}` yields the JSON value itself rather than its text. There is no escape sequence; a literal `${` is not expressible.

Template.description: Any JSON value. Strings render as `TemplateString`; objects and arrays render their values recursively, with keys left as written; numbers, bools and null pass through.

Predicate.description: A guard: one comparison, or `all`, `any` or `not` over other predicates. Comparison of unlike JSON types is false, never an error, and a path that resolves to nothing is treated as JSON null.

oneOf.description: One comparison of the value at `path` against `value`.

op.description: How to compare. `eq` and `ne` by JSON value, with `1` and `1.0` equal. `lt`, `lte`, `gt` and `gte` order numbers numerically and strings by code point. `in` is true when the value is equal to any element of the array in `value`. `exists` is true when the path names a value that is not null, and takes no `value`. `matches` applies the regular expression in `value` to a string; a pattern that does not compile is false. `ne` needs the same JSON type and a different value; write `{ "not": { "op": "eq" } }` for the test that is also true across types.

value.description: What to compare against. Required for every op but `exists`. An array for `in`, a string for `matches`, a number or a string for the ordering ops. A JSON null is a value, so `eq null` is a test for absent-or-null.

oneOf.description: True when every member is true. At least one member: an empty `all` would always be true, and a guard that always passes is a mistake.
True when at least one member is true. At least one member: an empty `any` would never be true, and the node it guards would never run.

RetryPolicy.description: How a claimable step is retried after a `retryable` failure. A `fatal`, `invalid_input` or `cancelled` failure is never retried. A worker's `retry_after_ms` is honoured when it is larger than the computed backoff.

max_attempts.description: How many attempts in total, counting the first. `1` means no retry.

backoff.description: How the wait before each retry grows. `fixed` waits `initial_ms` every time. `exponential` grows from `initial_ms` and never exceeds `max_ms`.

initial_ms.description: The wait before the second attempt, in milliseconds.

max_ms.description: The ceiling on any one wait, in milliseconds.

Limits.description: The ceilings a definition declares. A run that reaches one is ended `failed` with an error naming the ceiling. On a root run, `max_steps` and `max_cost_usd` bound the whole tree of subworkflows; a child's own limits also apply to it.

max_steps.description: How many steps the run tree may complete.

run_timeout_ms.description: How long the whole run may take, in milliseconds.

max_cost_usd.description: How much the run tree may spend, as priced by the daemon's price book from the usage workers report.

ClaimableNode.description: A `task` or `agent` node: the only kinds a branch, a foreach body or a loop body may be, because each of those is one claimable step in version 1.

TaskNode.description: Claimable work. The worker runs whatever code it registered under this id.

id.description: The step id. Unique within the document; the schema checks the spelling and the Rust validator checks the uniqueness. It names the step in `steps.<id>` paths, on leases and in the trace.

kind.description: Claimable work. The worker runs whatever code it registered under this id.

when.description: A guard. Evaluated when the cursor reaches the node. False writes an attempt row with status `skipped` and the cursor moves on. Absent means true.

on_error.description: What happens when the node fails after its retries. `fail_run` ends the run `failed` with the message. `continue` marks the step `failed` and advances, so a later `when` can read `steps.<id>.status` and `steps.<id>.error`.

input.description: Rendered per attempt and handed to the worker as the lease's `input`. Absent means the run's input.

effect.description: What a duplicated body would cost. Under `at_least_once` a lease that expires mid-body is requeued. Under `at_most_once` a started attempt whose outcome is unknown fails the run rather than running twice, and the worker must post `started` before `complete` or `fail`.

step_timeout_ms.description: Bounds one attempt in milliseconds, heartbeats or not. Absent means only the run's own deadline applies.

retry.description: How a `retryable` failure is retried. Absent means one attempt and no retry.

AgentNode.description: Claimable work, identical to `task` on the wire. The kind is recorded so the trace and the UI can tell an agent turn from a plain step. The worker resolves the body; the daemon does not care.

event.description: The event name an inbound `POST /v1/api/events` must carry.

key.description: Rendered per run, so `${input.order_id}` addresses this run and no other. The daemon matches `(project, event, key)` against live waits.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait, in milliseconds, before `on_timeout` applies.

accept_parked.description: Whether an event that arrived before the run reached this node counts. A parked event is consumed oldest first and is deleted after 24 hours.

on_timeout.description: What the wait does when its deadline passes. `fail` treats the passed deadline as the node failing, so `on_error` applies. `continue` moves the cursor on with no event delivered, so a later `when` can read `steps.<id>.status`.

ParallelNode.description: A fixed fan-out. Each branch is one claimable step keyed `<id>/<branch id>`, all on disk before any is offered. The node is done when every branch has ended; a branch that fails follows its own `on_error`, and `continue` lets the join finish.

id.description: The step id. Unique within the document; the schema checks the spelling and the Rust validator checks the uniqueness. It names the step in `steps.<id>` paths, on leases and in the trace.

branches.description: The branches. Each is a `task` or `agent` node; a multi-step branch is a `subworkflow`. Read a branch's result at `steps.<id>.<branch id>`.

ForeachNode.description: A fan-out over the items of an array. Each item becomes one attempt keyed `<id>[<index>]`. Afterwards `steps.<id>.outputs` is the array of item outputs in item order.

over.description: A path, not a template. It must resolve to a JSON array when the cursor reaches the node.

body.description: The `task` or `agent` run once per item. Its `input` template can read `item` and `index`. A multi-step body is a `subworkflow`.

concurrency.description: How many items are claimable at once.

max_items.description: An array longer than this fails the run, so a bad input cannot fan out without bound.

LoopNode.description: A bounded loop. Iteration `i` is keyed `<id>[<i>]/<body id>`. Afterwards `steps.<id>.outputs` is the array of iteration outputs.

body.description: The `task` or `agent` run each iteration. Inside it, `iter.index` is the iteration number and `steps.<body id>` is this iteration's attempt.

max_iterations.description: The bound. Required, because an unbounded loop is a run that never ends and no ceiling above it is cheaper than this one.

until.description: Evaluated after each iteration; true ends the loop. Absent means run `max_iterations` times.

SubworkflowNode.description: A child run. The child's output becomes `steps.<id>.output`. A child that ends `failed`, `timed_out` or `cancelled` fails the parent step, which then follows its `on_error`. Cancel walks down. `max_steps` and `max_cost_usd` on the root bound the whole tree.

version.description: Which version of the child to run. Absent pins the highest stored version at the parent's start, recorded in the parent run's `bindings`.

input.description: Rendered when the child starts and posted as its input. Absent means the parent's input.

Node.description: One node of the graph, told apart by `kind`. Every kind accepts `id`, `kind`, `when` and `on_error`; the claimable kinds also accept `input`, `effect`, `step_timeout_ms` and `retry`. `end` is never written: it is what the cursor names after the last node.

input.note: Refund of ${steps.order.output.amount_usd} USD for ${input.order_id} needs a person: ${steps.small_refund.error.message}

input.prompt: Tell the customer what happened with order ${input.order_id}.
